flaws.locator: Theorem 4.3, proof, the sentence 'The assumptions of Theorem 3.4 are then satisfied if we consider n to be k' and the application 'By applying Theorem 3.4, we deduce that pi(n) - m(n) = o(M(m(n)) sqrt(m(n))) a.c.': Theorem 3.4 is applied to pi(n) = sum f_p(i) as a sum of independent random variables (Section 3's standing assumption that omega'_1, ..., omega'_n are independent) on the strength of the paragraph after Proposition 4.1 - 'Furthermore, f_p(1), ..., f_p(n) are independent, and f_p(n) is determined by n' and 'the prime counting function ... behaves as the sum of the independent random variables' - which the notice calls unjustified, and of Proposition 4.1 (item 33) for the random-variable status
